title: Rust Host Agent cutover requires complete behavior parity evidence
claim: No Rust slice may receive production traffic or justify Go retirement until a provenance-bound manifest passes every CLI, schema/catalog, auth, MCP wire, provider, plan, durable-state, package, client, and isolated external-effect parity gate for the selected current Go revision. Missing, stale, malformed, or blocked evidence fails the gate. Cutover and Go retirement are separate decisions.
owner: The new host-agent Rust repository owns the parity manifest and verifier; the Host Agent, Platform, release, and deployment owners retain their respective cutover decisions.
rationale: A compiled binary, green unit tests, a health response, or a static tool list cannot establish that the replacement preserves an authenticated operational boundary or existing durable work.

included: all Host Agent modes, public capabilities, and configured provider projections
MCP, CLI, package, installation, and client behavior
plans, operations, observations, state conversion, and rollback
production cutover and subsequent Go retirement
excluded: new product capabilities, which require a separate OpenSpec delta
private deployment credentials and controller implementation

exception: No implicit exception. A different product contract requires a separately reviewed specification and owner decision. A blocked live test remains unverified and cannot be waived by a passing lower-level test.

required: exact Go source tree and current selected release/catalog revision
machine-readable parity inventory with supported modes and provider fixtures
differential CLI, schema/catalog, auth, and MCP wire results
provider lifecycle, Tasks/cancellation, plan, and durable-state results
isolated external-effect and rollback rehearsal results
published package and real client first-success results
Host Agent, Platform, release, and deployment owner cutover review
evidence.verifier: tools/parity/parity/verify.py (fail closed; negative tests in tools/parity/tests/test_verify.py)

revisionBehavior: A Go contract, package, mode, provider, schema, catalog, or transport revision change invalidates affected parity evidence and requires a reviewed source-lock and manifest rebase. A Rust implementation change reruns the affected gates and the whole-agent cutover verifier.

anchors.note: Pinned initial Go source and release/catalog provenance
Observable parity baseline and cutover requirement
Gates, evidence suites and one item per scenario

verificationStatus: Verifier implemented and fail closed. `make parity-verify-cutover` FAILS, as intended, until the inventory has no gaps (38 remain, all M8 or M10) and every reviewed cutoverEvidence file exists. Task 0.5 review recorded in `review`.

review.reviewer: Claude, performing task 0.5 at the owner's request

adrCoverage.0001 standalone MVP: read-only default and mutation flag: standalone-read-only-gate contract (D10) and the standalone catalog cells
adrCoverage.0002 provider extension, 0003 cloudflare: provider-lifecycle matrix, callback delegation scenarios and the D14 three-role seam
adrCoverage.0003 resource URIs, 0004 typed edges, 00: catalog descriptor and edge comparison per cell, admission binding scenarios
adrCoverage.0006 canonical identity: config validation matrix and agentId in every /health and catalog observation; Rust preserves OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID exactly
adrCoverage.0007 runtime kind, 0010 and 0014 storage: domain operations, owned by M8 and present as M8 inventory gaps
adrCoverage.0008 product-neutral transport: wire and auth scenarios; default listen ports are not observable in the harness, which always sets a port (finding 2)
adrCoverage.0009 catalog authority: catalog matrix, the provider cells, and catalog.unpublished-dispatch (dispatch names absent from the catalog are unreachable)
adrCoverage.0011 legacy handshake gate: wire and mcp scenarios with OPUTE_MCP_ALLOW_LEGACY_HANDSHAKE
adrCoverage.0013, 0015, 0016 k3s and HA networking: k3s and tailscale provider journeys and the recipe corpus; their domain execution is M8

findings.finding: The cutover gate checked differential suites, canaries, contracts, oracles, M5 and inventory gaps, but none of the required evidence no suite produces: published package and real client first success, isolated external effects, rollback rehearsal, and the owners' cutover review. Once the inventory reached zero gaps it could have passed without them.
findings.resolution: verify.py rule requireCutoverEvidence: the cutover gate requires each reviewed file in manifest.cutoverEvidence, pinned by hash; negative test test_cutover_requires_each_reviewed_cutover_evidence_file

findings.finding: ADR 0008 default listen addresses (standalone 127.0.0.1:3014, platform 0.0.0.0:3004) are never observed, because every harness profile sets HOST_MCP_PORT.
findings.resolution: owned by the packageFirstSuccess cutover evidence, which runs the published launcher on its defaults (M10)

findings.finding: ADR 0012's /health mcpToolNamePrefix and the release-parity decision's launcher-local identity were not observed.
The D13 evidence-redaction contract ran in every cycle but the cutover gate did not require it.
findings.resolution: added to the cutover gate's requireContracts and the manifest contracts

review.outcome: The invariant is preserved as written, with no product capability introduced and none retired. Its verifier is active and fails closed. The Host Agent, Platform, release and deployment owners' review of an actual cutover remains a separate decision, recorded as the ownerReview cutover evidence.
